trust_decision.summary: Header-supplied 32-bit sizes/offsets in an untrusted .lit file (hdrLen, nPieces, secHdrLen and later contentOffset / entry offset+size / atom sizes) are trusted as in-bounds after signed-int arithmetic; LitDoc.cpp decides in-bounds via `x + n > len` comparisons that wrap.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'LIT header parsing' integer overflow; LitParseHeader computes off = hdrLen + nPieces*16 and builds Str(d.s + off) without bounding hdrLen.

fix_sites.entry_point: CreateEngineLitFromFile -> LitToEpubConvert (open a .lit file; also test_engines CLI)
CreateEngineLitFromFile -> LitToEpubConvert (open a .lit file; also test_engines CLI)
fix_sites.module_kind: low-level bounds-checked reader helper (LitU32, used by LitU64 and every parser)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/LitDoc.cpp:310-324 (LitU16/LitU32 helpers' own off+N comparison, shared by all LIT parsers)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The helpers already check off < 0 and only overflow for off within 4 of INT_MAX, so a solver bounding hdrLen in LitParseHeader can argue the helpers are already 'bounds-checked' and the report is about the header.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate .lit files with secHdrLen larger than the remaining file are accepted (sec is clamped with std::min), and directory entries whose junk root '/' value saturates to INT_MAX via LitEncInt must still parse; an over-broad fix rejecting large/saturated values or secHdrLen > remaining breaks real books.

O6_input_shapes: hdrLen near INT_MAX / with high bit set (negative after (int) cast)
offsets within 2/4 bytes of INT_MAX passed to LitU16/LitU32

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Secondary-header block loop: pos from LitU32(sec,4) near INT_MAX makes pos + 8 wrap negative, passing the bound before Str blockTag(sec.s + pos, 4) is read
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same function as the fix, but the fix only bounds hdrLen/secHdrLen and the loop already has 'pos >= 0' so it looks guarded
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function, 2 lines below the fixed check

O8_uncovered_routes.route: contentOffset read from the ITSF block as (int)LitU32 can be negative; GetFile section 0 computes off = contentOffset + e->offset and only checks the upper bound before Str(d.s + off)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Arithmetic already done in i64, so it looks overflow-safe; the flaw is the missing lower bound, which a solver can call 'not an overflow'
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, GetFile ~90 lines from landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GetFile compressed section: e->offset + e->size in int; both can be INT_MAX via LitEncInt saturation, wrapping negative and passing the check before Str(sec.s + e->offset)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Directory-entry lookup, not 'header parsing'; values come from the 7-bit encoded directory, which a solver may treat as a separate feature

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Atom table: size = (int)LitU32 up to INT_MAX, pos + size wraps negative, passing the check before Str(data.s + pos, size)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Content-level tokenized-HTML atom parsing, far from the container header the report names
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~540 lines from landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: LZX reset-table ofsEntry/size arithmetic feeding content.s + base into LZXdecompress
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ofsEntry is (int)LitU32 + 8 and size bounds are hand-written per field; a maintainer could easily drop the size < base or size > len(content) leg.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Section name list using a 32-bit length instead of LitU16 so pos + nChars*2 + 2 can wrap
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same additive 'pos + n > len' idiom used throughout; widening the field read is a plausible edit.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ControlData csize = (LitU32+1)*4 signed multiply overflow used to slice control
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Existing code already relies on csize <= 0 catching overflow; a wrap to a small positive value is realistic.

O9_family: integer overflow / signed wrap in bounds check leading to out-of-bounds (invalid-pointer) read in a binary container parser

O10_build.toolchain: premake5 + Visual Studio 2022 (Windows); a mingw build script exists (cmd/helper/mingw-build.ts); test_engines CLI target includes LitDoc.cpp
O10_build.project_tests: No LIT tests or .lit fixtures in the pinned tree; src/tools/test_engines.cpp can open a .lit via CreateEngineLitFromFile (src/tools/test_engines.cpp:65-66). LitToEpubConvert (src/LitDoc.h:7) is a pure buffer->buffer function suitable for a harness.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `hdrLen + nPieces*16 > len(d)` (in i64) in LitParseHeader and stop, leaving the pos+8 loop, negative contentOffset in GetFile, offset+size in sections and atom sizes open.
